part_text: (1a) On 26 November 2025, the European Parliament adopted a recommendation on the EU's diplomatic strategy and geopolitical cooperation in the Arctic. / (1b) On 7 June 2023, the Commission and the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy adopted a joint communication on a New Agenda for Relations between the EU and Latin America and the Caribbean. / (2a) The allocation of financial resources between the OCTs should be based on transparent and verifiable criteria by which the European added value of the expenditure can be assessed. Those criteria should take into account the structural constraints of the OCTs and should reflect the diversity of realities, demographics, vulnerabilities and priorities that characterises each territory, as well as the needs of OCTs and the contribution of Union funding to connectivity, to regional integration, to maritime security, to the oversight of exclusive economic zones, to the resilience of critical infrastructure and to securing supply chains, including critical raw material supply chains. / (3) The strategic focus, coherence and flexibility of the Programme and the policy dialogue framework of the Decision should be further enhanced to ensure more impact and focus on sustainable outcomes, while delivering on the objectives of the association of the Union with the OCTs. / (3a) Clear, reliable and transparent indicative sub-envelopes contribute to budgetary predictability, transparency in programming and support rigorous assessments whether or not the stated objectives are achieved. / (3b) There is a need for a dialogue between the Union and the OCTs with a view to clarifying and explaining the scope, and facilitating the implementation, of horizontal, trade-related Union instruments, including, in particular, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. / (4) In a rapidly changing economic, social and geopolitical environment, recent experience has shown the need for a more flexible multiannual financial framework and Union spending programmes. To that effect, and in line with the objectives of the association, the funding should duly consider the evolving, current and future policy needs and the Union’s priorities as identified in relevant documents published by the Commission, in Council conclusions and European Parliament resolutions while ensuring sufficient predictability for the budget implementation. Flexibility in spending should be accompanied by clear priorities, result-oriented implementation and transparent reporting, in order to ensure predictability, accountability and the effective use of Union funding. / (5) The implementation of the amended Decision (EU) 2021/1764 should support cooperation, including under the Global Gateway strategy3, the Union’s external investment strategy to advance high environmental, social and governance standards, in line with the 360-degree approach, and more broadly the sustainable development goals together with partner countries and territories, and the Union's objectives in connectivity, economic security, and geopolitical positioning. Complementarities between actions under the Global Gateway strategy and its toolbox, the European Competitiveness Fund and other relevant Union instruments should be strengthened to help unlock investment opportunities in the OCTs, positively impact their safety, contribute to building more robust and self-sufficient local economies, create quality employment, stimulate innovation, improve overall living standards, and promote their more effective integration into Union’s regional cooperation frameworks, while ensuring that funding under this Decision remains focused on the sustainable development needs of the OCTs and delivers tangible benefits for local communities. \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 3 Joint Communication to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and Social Committee, the Committee of the Regions and the European Investment Bank - The Global …
